DSH COMPOSITE IDENTITY — issue #226 task 8.8 parts (a)–(c): make the delivered branch green on macOS. Branch slice-dsh-composite-b; adopt every commit. This is a PORTABILITY repair of an already-judged delivery, not a redesign.

WHERE THIS STANDS. Run dsh-composite-identity-issue-226-e291e076 completed; its council established no medium-or-higher defect, no security residual and no specification defect. The branch is open as PR #311. CI on that PR: ubuntu tests, exact coverage, clippy, MSRV, packaging all PASS. `test (macos-latest)` FAILS with twelve tests, all in crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite/tests.rs and tests/native_matrix.rs. The verbatim failure lines from the CI log are in .forge/tasks/controller-macos-ci-failures-pr311-2026-09-21.txt — READ IT FIRST. There is no macOS host here: that file is your only observation of macOS, so reason from it and from the platform's documented behaviour, and say plainly which fixes are proved on Linux and which can only be proved by the PR's macOS leg.

THE TWELVE, grouped by cause as the controller reads the log (verify each; do not take the grouping on faith):
A. /var vs /private/var. macOS's temp dir is a symlink; production canonicalises and the test expects the uncanonicalised spelling (or the reverse). Tests: removing_only_the_plugin_manifest_names_the_drifted_file (5161), the_root_package_lock_is_never_read_beside_or_instead_of_the_hidden_one (8788), native_matrix (1250), and probably the_core_manifest_and_hidden_lock_are_read_once_and_retained (8343: opened-once counter reads 0, likely a path-keyed counter missing on spelling), the_core_executable_must_be_lib_bin_js_with_the_exact_shebang (1674), an_unreadable_npm_lock_and_extension… (1697), a_bundle_candidate_that_cannot_be_inspected… (1568). The rule: a test builds its expectation from the same spelling production reports — canonicalise the fixture root once where the fixture is made — never by string-gluing a temp path.
B. errno numbers. the_lookup_rule_is_each_librarys_own_switch_arm_by_arm (7044) expects "(os error 40)"; ELOOP is 62 on macOS. Build the expected text from the platform's own io::Error for that errno constant, never a literal number.
C. The reported NAME. an_empty_path_entry… (2128, 2214) and an_absent_path_is_a_named_refusal… (3163): macOS reports "./mytool" where Linux reports "mytool". This one may be PRODUCTION behaviour differing by platform, not a test artefact. Find which code path prefixes "./" on macOS, decide from the specification which spelling the refusal owes, and make production say the same thing on both platforms unless the spec gives a platform-qualified reason. Prove by removal.
D. env -S wording. the_candidate_classifier… (5544): macOS yields "which is not the measured `env <program>` form" where the test expects the "splits into more than the one word" reason. The spec already platform-qualifies env -S; make the test's expectation follow the platform arm the production code takes, and confirm the production arm is the one the spec assigns to Apple.
E. Non-UTF-8 file names. the_plugin_walk_refuses_a_name_that_is_not_utf8 (7625): APFS refuses to create such a name (EILSEQ, os error 92), so the fixture cannot be built. Where the filesystem refuses the fixture, the test proves the refusal it can on that platform and says so; it does not unwrap the creation.

RULES. Linux behaviour and every Linux assertion stay exactly as judged — a fix that weakens a Linux assertion to make macOS pass is a regression. Assert reasons, never is_err(). Prove each production change by removal. Do NOT add Windows handling of any kind: decision 0063 (accepted 2026-09-21) — Windows is not a host, and the e291e076 LOW about a windows-msvc clippy lint is closed by that decision, not by code.

GATES, crate-scoped and sequential, never a boxed workspace run: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; every crate suite green; openspec validate --all --strict. State what the box could not execute.

DO NOT TICK 8.8. Parts (a)–(c) only. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/, docs/decisions/ do not move; 0056 stays proposed. Record what you delivered, and list per test whether the fix is Linux-proved or awaits the macOS leg.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
```

result.notes: Framing: .forge/tasks/dsh-macos-portability.md. Ruled chore: the twelve failures support bounded portability maintenance of the already-judged 8.8(a)-(c) delivery, with fixture/expectation repairs and a narrow cwd-refusal display-name correction preserving native lookup semantics. No new contract, core/store or policy design is required. Verified the supplied log against code; the env -S summary reverses actual and expected, and the non-UTF-8 panic excerpt omits the errno payload. Framing names all twelve tests, expected files, removal proof, sequential crate gates, frozen surfaces and pending native macOS evidence. No implementation or delivery tests performed; 8.8 stays unchecked.

Repaired the twelve macOS failures of PR #311 on slice-dsh-composite-b, adopting every commit. Five causes. (A) /var vs /private/var: a test-side FixtureRoot canonicalizes the temporary root once at creation and retains the TempDir for cleanup; Synthetic, the core-executable test's two independent roots and the native-matrix parent build on it. (B) ELOOP: the expected rendering is built from the host's io::Error for the same Errno::LOOP constant (40 on Linux, 62 on Darwin); the other errnos in that table agree across both hosts and keep their literals. (C) the only production change: Search::refuse_working_directory renders the named cwd refusal from the SEARCHED NAME, because glibc and musl build the bare name for an empty entry while Apple builds ./<name>, so one rule was being reported two ways; the native STOP at that candidate is untouched and still names the candidate as the platform built it. Every Linux string is byte-identical. (D) env -S: the two multiword vectors follow env_program's compile-time kernel arm, as the neighbouring node --flag case already did, plus two new single-word vectors so the measured-form refusal has a vector on every platform; the commission's summary reversed actual and expected and the production arm was already right. (E) non-UTF-8 name: the fixture's creation is answered rather than unwrapped, asserting Errno::ILSEQ and the missing entry where the filesystem refuses it. No Linux assertion weakened, no Windows handling added (0063). Removal proofs on this Linux host: restoring candidate.display() fails the new every-library test on its Library::Apple row with exactly the CI excerpt's ./mytool-vs-mytool mismatch; and under a TMPDIR whose spelling is not its canonical one, removing the canonicalization fails exactly the seven fixture-spelling tests the macOS leg reports, in the same shape (103 pass / 96 pass 7 fail / 103 pass). Groups B, D and E have no Linux removal control and are recorded as awaiting the macOS leg. Gates run and clean: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings, all seven crate suites crate-scoped and sequential (0 failed), cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self; the full native matrix executed (997 oracles, 128 working-directory refusals). NOT EXECUTED and not passes: openspec validate --all --strict and bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh, both refused launch by this seat's sandbox; the coverage gate is unchanged and the production delta adds no branch or function. One intermittent ETXTBSY loss (#255) on a first protocol run, green on rerun. Two signed commits, nothing pushed: 7d979a51 (code) and a7c07cd1 (tasks account). 8.8 stays unchecked; part (d) untouched; frozen paths, extensions/dsh/ and docs/decisions/ have no diff and 0056 stays proposed. Full account with logs in .forge/tasks/dsh-macos-portability-evidence.md and in the tasks.md section dated 2026-09-21. The repaired head's own test (macos-latest) leg is required before the branch can be called green on macOS.

result.notes:

Surviving finding — LOW, author: correctness; independently confirmed by chief. crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite/tests.rs:7803 uses raw.symlink_metadata().is_err() to claim the rejected non-UTF-8 name left no entry. Any metadata error satisfies that assertion, violating the commission's explicit reason-specific assertion rule and contradicting the delivery record's claim that no is_err() was introduced. Assert the specific metadata cause or directly assert the directory's entry names. Creation already asserts Errno::ILSEQ and the subsequent exact-membership walk limits the impact. This is one deduplicated test-assertion finding, not a production security defect. No additional chief finding, medium-or-higher defect, security residual, or specification defect was established.

Inspected canonical-root removal/restoration logs: exactly the seven reported path tests fail without canonicalization, then all 103 composite tests pass restored under noncanonical TMPDIR.
